parts.context: Two colleagues plan an online induction for a support team.

script.speaker: Mira
script.text: We need to plan the online induction for the new support team. More and more colleagues are working from home, so a remote session would help everyone attend. I suggest starting at half past nine on Thursday. The trainer can explain our internal forum first, and then everyone can ask questions. Could you test the equipment before the session begins?

script.speaker: Theo
script.text: Yes. I checked the microphone this morning, and it works well. The camera picture disappeared twice because its cable was loose. I have replaced the cable, and the picture is steady now. If we had a second camera, we would have a spare for important sessions. I will ask the manager about that later.

script.speaker: Mira
script.text: Good idea. Please send a short survey on Friday so we can learn what the new colleagues think. We should ask whether the instructions were clear and whether they could hear the trainer. Next month, I would like to allow more time for follow-up questions. A longer presentation would not necessarily make the training better.

script.speaker: Theo
script.text: Agreed. I will prepare the survey today and send the meeting invitation after lunch.

parts.context: Rosa announces a customer service workshop.

script.speaker: Rosa
script.text: Welcome to our short announcement about next week's customer service workshop. The workshop is on Tuesday, and it starts at ten in the morning. Please come to room twelve on the second floor. We are using a small room because each person needs time to try the new online ordering service. Bring your headphones, but you do not need to bring a laptop because the room already has computers. First, the trainer will show how to choose an item and confirm the delivery address. Then you will practise with a partner using a sample customer account. Please use the training account, not your personal account. If you have trouble signing in, contact the help desk before the workshop starts. They can reset your details and check that you have permission to use the service. At the end, each pair will give a summary lasting two minutes about one problem they solved. It would be great to know which steps you find difficult, so write your questions on the shared page. We will use those questions to improve the next workshop.

questions.explanation: Rosa hướng dẫn liên hệ help desk nếu đăng nhập gặp lỗi.

questions.explanation: Mỗi cặp trình bày phần tổng kết trong two minutes.

passage.title: A trial of a staff forum
paragraphs: Rivergate Design is a small company with staff in three towns. Last spring, its managers noticed that employees were sending the same questions by email every week. Replies often reached only the person who asked, so useful advice was difficult for others to find. The company decided to try a private staff forum for two weeks before choosing a permanent service.

During the trial, each team appointed a mentor who welcomed new users and answered simple questions. Employees could search earlier discussions or start a new topic. The most helpful replies came from experienced colleagues who explained a task in plain language. New starters valued these replies because they included practical examples rather than unexplained technical words. Mentors wrote a short weekly summary so that staff who had missed a discussion could catch up quickly.

Managers also set clear expectations. The forum was for work questions, and personal customer details had to stay in approved systems. Nobody was required to read messages outside working hours. Staff could still telephone a colleague when an issue was urgent. A popular suggestion was to rotate the mentor role each month, giving several people a chance to share their knowledge.

After the trial, the company counted unanswered questions and asked employees about their experience. It did not judge success by the number of posts alone. If the service helped people solve real problems faster, the managers would keep it. They planned another review after three months to check whether the improvement lasted.

To make repeated work advice easier to find

passage.title: A studio tests video meetings
paragraphs: North Lane Studio is testing video meetings with two partner teams. Before the trial, most discussions took place by telephone. Designers sometimes misunderstood a change because they could not see the same drawing. The studio now holds two online sessions each week, with one person sharing a picture on the screen. Each session lasts thirty minutes, and a coordinator sends a short list of topics in advance.

The partners can join from their existing laptops; they do not have to buy new computers. Participants should use a quiet place and test their sound before joining. Some people prefer to listen first and ask questions at the end, which is allowed. The coordinator invites only named team members and checks each person before admitting them. Invitations are not published on an open website.

The studio is collecting comments during the six-week trial. If sound quality improved, the partners would consider more frequent sessions. However, the manager will wait until the trial ends before deciding whether to expand the service. Short written notes remain available for colleagues who cannot attend.

email.task: Write an email of 80–100 words to Sam explaining how to attend a remote training session. Include all the steps below, one polite request and a second conditional sentence about a possible improvement.
bullets: Open the training application and sign in
Enter the session code from the invitation
Select Join and wait for the trainer
Use the hand button to ask a question
Leave at the end and send feedback
email.modelAnswer:
Dear Sam,
Here are the steps for your remote training session. First, open the training application and sign in. Check your microphone and camera before you start. Next, enter the session code from the invitation. Select Join and wait for the trainer to admit you. During the session, use the hand button if you want to ask a question. Finally, leave the session and send your feedback. Could you tell me if anything is unclear? If we had more time, we would practise together beforehand.
Best wishes,
Alex

parts.instructions: Explain the trend using the cues. Include a polite training request.
parts.prompt: Your team is using a private discussion group more frequently. Explain the change and ask for training.
cues: Describe what more colleagues are doing
Explain how communication is becoming easier
Ask the trainer how to search earlier discussions
requiredGrammar: Polite request with Could someone tell me
parts.sampleAnswer: More and more colleagues are sharing questions in our private group. People are answering each other more quickly, and communication is becoming easier. New users can learn from earlier discussions, but they need clear instructions. Could someone tell me how to search for a topic? It would be great to know how to mark a useful reply as well.

parts.instructions: Give a proposal using at least two second conditional sentences and a polite request.
parts.prompt: Your manager is considering video meetings with another office. Explain two possible benefits and politely ask for a trial.
cues: Explain how teams could see the same picture
Request a short trial before buying the service
requiredGrammar: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + infinitive
parts.sampleAnswer: If we used video meetings, we would spend less time travelling to the other office. If both teams shared a picture on screen, they would understand design changes more clearly. We should test the sound and allow time for questions. Could we arrange a short trial before buying the service? If the trial worked well, we would have better evidence for our decision.
